title: Travelling India slowly
standfirst: India punishes the circuit and rewards the single base. How we build a fortnight that leaves you rested rather than wrung out.

blocks.heading: The country is not the unit of travel here
paras: The usual mistake is treating India as one destination. It is roughly the size of Europe and about as internally various, and a week spent crossing it is a week spent in transit.
We plan by state, and usually by one or two states. A member with twelve nights sees Rajasthan properly, or the Kerala coast and the Western Ghats, and leaves with something to come back for.

blocks.heading: Houses rather than hotels
blocks.caption: A private house taken whole, with its own staff.
paras: The best rooms in India are frequently not in hotels. Family palaces, tea bungalows, coastal houses and farmhouses take guests privately, with their own cooks and their own rhythm.
For any stay over four nights we look at a house before a hotel. It costs less than the equivalent suite, and it gives a family or a group of friends the run of the place.

blocks.heading: The parks, and how to do them
blocks.caption: Tiger country: two parks, four days, one naturalist throughout.
paras: Tiger sightings are a matter of patience and of having the right naturalist, not of luck. Park permits are released months ahead and the good zones go first.
We book permits before dates are confirmed elsewhere, and we keep the same naturalist with a member across both parks so the second one starts where the first left off.

blocks.heading: Questions members ask
blocks.intro: The ones that come up nearly every time.

a: October to March across most of the country. The hill stations and Ladakh reverse that entirely and open from April to September, so a summer trip goes up rather than across.

items.q: How much moving is too much?
a: One base per week is our rule, with day journeys out. Members who insist on four cities in ten nights usually tell us afterwards that they remember the airports.

items.q: Is a private vehicle worth it?
a: Yes, and we would not plan India without one. A driver who knows the state rather than the country is the single biggest difference between a smooth fortnight and a tiring one.

blocks.heading: We are ready when you are
paras: Every itinerary starts with a conversation about what you actually want from the days, and works backwards to houses, guides and timing from there.
